ruling-unicode-16-digit-versioned-rule.reason: Adopt for #232, part of #156, porting bench/tools/ruling_record.py, ruling_summary.py and delegation.py to bench-tools ruling. Diagnostics keep the Python program names, so saved output stays identical. Records an intended difference from older interpreters, by the repository owner's direction for #154, delegated through the migration's orchestration. Old behavior: ruling_record.kept matched a versioned rule name with \.v\d+\., so the digits it accepted depended on the interpreter's Unicode database. New behavior: bench-tools ruling matches \d with pytext::decimal_value, fixed at the Unicode 16.0 decimal digits (category Nd) Python 3.14 matches, for a pinned result that does not depend on the interpreter. Compatibility impact: against Python 3.12, which CI uses (Unicode 15.0), the 80 decimal digits added in Unicode 16.0 (U+10D40..U+10D49, U+116D0..U+116E3, U+11BF0..U+11BF9, U+16130..U+16139, U+16D70..U+16D79, U+1CCF0..U+1CCF9, U+1E5F1..U+1E5FA). Older interpreters lack more: Python 3.10 (Unicode 13.0) lacks 110, those 80 and 30 added in Unicode 14.0 and 15.0 (U+11F50..U+11F59, U+16AC0..U+16AC9, U+1E4F0..U+1E4F9). No tracked ruling record, round file, opening or pinned path contains any of the 110. This case pins a rule outside docs/research named rule.v\U0001e5f1.md: on Python 3.13 or older (Unicode 15.1 or earlier), check refused it as a file edited in place, exit 1, which baseline_defect records from Python 3.12; Rust accepts it, as Python 3.14 does. Resolving issue: #232.
